Summary:
Mr. Robert Yu is a 70-year-old male under care for prostate cancer, which was diagnosed on February 8, 2023. At the time of diagnosis, the Gleason score was 8, indicating a moderately high-grade cancer. He underwent treatment approximately 2.1 years ago, and the cancer is currently controlled. He is on leuprolide 22.5 mg as part of his ongoing management.

On his most recent visit on August 21, 2024, Mr. Yu presented for follow-up related to his prostate cancer. His blood pressure was 148/76 mmHg, and his weight was 114 pounds. The physical exam was largely unremarkable, with normal findings in the cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams. He reported no new symptoms or concerns related to his cancer. 

Mr. Yu has had consistent follow-up visits since his diagnosis. His most recent laboratory tests, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA), showed no signs of recurrence. His weight has remained relatively stable over the past year, ranging between 103 and 115 pounds.

His social history includes alcohol consumption of approximately 2 drinks per week. He does not report tobacco use. Mr. Yu's family history is significant for his father, who had hypertension onset at age 68 and is currently alive at age 82.

Management Plan:
- Continue leuprolide 22.5 mg
- Routine follow-up for prostate cancer every 3-6 months
- Regular monitoring of PSA levels
- Annual physical exams and vaccinations as needed

Mr. Yu remains compliant with his treatment regimen and continues to monitor his condition closely. His overall health status is stable, and he has no active complaints related to his cancer. His blood pressure and weight have remained within normal limits throughout his follow-up visits.
